_about: Machine-readable twin of docs/digest/synthesis.md. Derived only from data/digest/PSI-*.json. Citation index for section findings is the 1-based position in the record findings list; for limitations/gaps/open_questions it is the 1-based list position; null means the whole section.

key_messages.text: Without buoyancy the flammability of a solid depends on ventilation speed: the boundary in O2 against flow is U-shaped, with a minimum at flows of about 1-10 cm/s. At that minimum PMMA rods burned down to 13.5% O2, against 15.4% for upward burning in 1 g with an extra 4 cm/s of forced flow. The boundary was mapped on one rod geometry and one fabric.

Normal-gravity screening does not bound flammability in orbit for every material and configuration. The comparisons below are with downward (opposed-flow) burning in 1 g, not with the upward-burning Test 1 itself; for Test 1 the investigators only suggest that it may act as an ignition test. SIBAL fabric that cannot burn downward in 1 g spread against 9-25 cm/s flows in orbit. Opposed spread over PMMA rods persisted to about 17-17.5% O2, against 18-19% in 1 g (sources disagree on the exact values). Near-limit ignition took up to 230 s, against the roughly 25 s Test 1 igniter time.

For the fire-retarded and silicone materials flown (Ultem, Nomex HT90-40, silicone), Test 1 was conservative at about 21-22% O2 and 15-20 cm/s (one sample per condition). Nomex III gave contradictory results near its 1-g limit.

Under forced ventilation, concurrent flames reach a bounded size and steady spread instead of accelerating. A 41 x 94 cm fabric sheet spread at 1.8 mm/s with a 40 mm flame and about 1.2 kW at 20 cm/s, and at 2.3 mm/s at 25 cm/s. Thick PMMA stayed anchored at a limiting size.
Small glovebox ducts overstate concurrent spread compared with large enclosures, attributed to flow acceleration from hot-gas expansion.

Quiescent microgravity flames are weak but persistent. They survive until radiative loss cools them to about 1100-1200 K, several hundred kelvin below 1-g extinction temperatures, and larger flames die sooner.

Stopping ventilation extinguished small flames in air, but emulated condensed-fuel flames burned steadily for minutes in quiescent 26.5-40% O2. Hot thermoplastics also keep emitting fuel vapour after extinction.

Inert-gas margins are smaller in orbit. The droplet LOI in N2 is 0.12 (methanol) and 0.15 (n-heptane), as much as 2-3 points below 1 g. CO2 raised it to 0.14 and 0.17, and He to 0.14 and 0.15. Modelling indicates xenon would be a poor agent.

Visible extinction is not the end of reaction. Cool flames (about 700 K in simulations) follow radiative extinction of n-alkane droplets and of gaseous n-butane flames. Above about 2 atm they often re-ignite a hot flame, and a catalytic surface can do the same.

Non-buoyant flames are sootier, cooler and more radiative: 4-8 times the 1-g soot, about 200 K cooler soot, and a radiative fraction about an order of magnitude higher (simulation). Smoke emission depends on ventilation speed and fuel-jet size.

Pre-ignition smoke from spacecraft materials is sub-micrometre (diameter of average mass about 0.1-0.5 um) and coarsens with aging and stagnation. The ISS light-scattering detector stayed below its alarm level for most Kapton and Teflon smokes. At 8 cm/s or more, flight and ground sizes matched. Single-moment detectors are inadequate.

Exploration atmospheres (30% O2 or more at 70.3 kPa or less) are untested for solid materials: every solid burn was near 1 atm at 22.7% O2 or less. The nearest data are gas-burner emulation at 34% O2 and 56 kPa (steady burning) and droplets at 30-34% O2 and 0.7 atm (no extinction).

gaps.gap: Solid materials at elevated O2 and reduced pressure
gaps.why: Habitats and rovers are planned at 30% O2 or more and 70.3 kPa or less; no solid flight data exist above 22.7% O2 or below 96 kPa.
gaps.partial_fill: BRE emulation maps; FLEX droplets at 0.7 atm, 30-34% O2; Saffire-II 1-g reduced-pressure correlation; CFI-G 40% O2 at 0.5 atm; PSI-62 model runs.

gaps.why: Weak lunar and Martian buoyant flows may sit near the most flammable region of the U-curve; there is no partial-gravity data in PSI.
gaps.partial_fill: E-FIELD ion-wind analogue; mixed-convection velocity correlation with explicit g; zero-stretch extrapolation of 1-g blow-off; gravity-switch simulations.

gaps.gap: Unreduced imagery and raw signals; no per-test outcomes
gaps.why: Terabytes of images and 125 Hz voltages hold burn times, flame radii and extinction modes that no table records.
gaps.partial_fill: ACME-DOC-010 in PSI-23 Reference Data can convert PSI-10 and PSI-159 voltages; BASS-II O2 table and fan calibrations; CFI analysed spreadsheet.

gaps.gap: Results held outside PSI or unpublished
gaps.why: BRE, CLD, E-FIELD, FLEX-2, SLICE and Saffire-II have only summary tables; s-Flame has no ISS paper; Flame Design pressure round not analysed in any PSI document; many findings rest on theses and slides.
gaps.partial_fill: External theses and NTRS documents already cited in the records.

gaps.gap: Pressure effects on solid spread and limits
gaps.why: Reduced pressure changes residence time, radiative loss and buoyancy-equivalent flow; no solid flight data off 1 atm.
gaps.partial_fill: Saffire-II 1-g reduced-pressure data; BRE and CFI-G pressure trends.

gaps.gap: Suppression with realistic agents and geometry
gaps.why: Only a fixed upstream N2 jet and well-mixed diluents were tested; no extinguisher discharge or water mist.
gaps.partial_fill: BASS N2 outcome matrix; re-derived FLEX LOIs.

gaps.why: SAME covered only pre-ignition pyrolysis; detector timing not analysed.
gaps.partial_fill: Cygnus smoke-detector and CO2 telemetry from Saffire-I/III; SAME-R time series.

gaps.why: Mostly PMMA and one cellulosic fabric; few repeats; no clutter, foams or wire insulation in flaming tests.
